text:
mike: Heads-up — customer A reported Dedicated cluster showing 0 GPUs in Console after we applied the nodepool relabel earlier today. They’re getting allocation failures on their jobs, e.g. 503s from the allocation API. Can someone from platform look?

jules: Customer on a reserved Dedicated account, escalated via support. They pasted a screenshot: dashboard shows node count 3, GPU count 0. Support say instances are running in cloud console.

sara: I can take a look. Quick question: was this the relabel that changed `nodepool=dedicated-01` -> `pool=dedicated-1`?

mike: yes that’s the one, rolled via Terraform at ~10:02 UTC (deploy-bot showed success).

deploy-bot: Rollout completed: terraform apply (plan 2024-11-07) — changed label on instance group `cluster-prod-eu-west/ig-3`

priya: If the inventory service keys off `nodepool` label, that would explain it. Inventory job reconciles by label, not instance-group id. I can grep the last inventory sync logs.

nate: Repro steps I used locally against staging: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-1 -o wide` returns nodes, but `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=dedicated-01` returns nothing. Console inventory query is `SELECT count(gpu_id) FROM node_inventory WHERE labels @> 'nodepool=dedicated-01'` — it’s returning 0.

jules: Customer is asking for ETA. Support flagged it as P2 since it’s affecting allocations.

priya: Workaround: we can relabel the nodes back to `nodepool=dedicated-01` or update inventory mapping to accept `pool` alias. I recommend reconciling inventory first so we don’t have to modify customer nodes.

sara: Steps I’m running now:
```
# check recent inventory sync job
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/inventory-sync --since=2h | tail -n 200
# show label distribution
kubectl get nodes --show-labels | egrep 'dedicated-0|dedicated-1' | sed -n '1,50p'
# quick DB check
psql redwood_meta -c "SELECT labels, count(*) FROM node_inventory WHERE cluster='cluster-prod-eu-west' GROUP BY labels;"
```

mike: Paste any logs here. Also please confirm whether the router fallback to hosted is working for the affected customer. They reported higher latency when allocations fail.

priya: Inventory-sync log excerpt: "WARN missing expected label 'nodepool' for node ip-10-2-3-4, labels present: pool=dedicated-1,role=inference" — looks like the sync treats label keys strictly. I’m going to trigger a manual reconcile: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/inventory-sync -- /app/bin/inv-sync --reconcile --cluster cluster-prod-eu-west`.

sara: Manual reconcile started. ETA ~2m.

deploy-bot: Job inv-sync (manual) started by priya at 2024-11-07T10:48:12Z

nate: Quick patch we can do if reconcile fails: add a compatibility rule in inventory service config: `label_aliases: { 'pool': ['nodepool'] }` so queries for `nodepool` will match `pool`. That avoids relabing nodes.

priya: Reconcile finished — logs show it mapped `pool=dedicated-1` -> `nodepool=dedicated-01` in the inventory projection for 3 nodes. DB query now shows GPUs count > 0.

jules: Support: I told customer we’re reconciling and to retry allocations. Please confirm customer can allocate and we’ll close.

mike: Customer confirmed allocations succeeding and latency dropped back to normal. Thanks all. Follow-ups: (1) add label aliasing to inventory service, (2) add a preflight check in Terraform plan to warn when renaming critical labels, (3) add an alert for sudden GPU count drop in Console for dedicated clusters.

sara: Filed infra ticket INF-1291 for label aliasing and Terraform hook. Also filed ALERT-402 to create Console metric alert.

jules: Closing the P2 with customer notified. :white_check_mark:

mike: Great response. Recommend runbook update so oncall knows to check label changes first for these inventory-desync symptoms.
